chapter: Meeting Louis and the New Orleans bands
title: Joining Jack Carey's band and starting his own band as Punch
summary: Punch briefly played with another band, then joined Carey; people mistook him for Carey, so the men quit and formed a band under his own name.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What about, who did Doc Ernest have on trumpet then?
Well, I was just a fights band I played with.

But I didn't stay with him for maybe a week, because Jack Kerry would come out there, and everybody was talking about Jack Kerry, you know. So I said, I believe I joined Jack Kerry. And I joined Jack Kerry. And I joined Jack Kerry. And I went on up. He had a big name. He had a big name. And after that, the boy, let me tell you this, you see. You see, everybody, leader of a band was a trumpet player. Keith Rennie, Buddy Patee, Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly, all of them were trumpet players. That's all your bunch? Now wait, now no. In a different band. So everybody, people didn't know me, they thought I was Jack Kerry. See, everybody around there called me Jack Kerry, but I wasn't Jack Kerry. Jack Kerry was the trombone player. See, he did the trombone player. See, he did the trombone player. So the boy said, look, Princey, you getting all that felicity for somebody else, you ought to let it go out in your name for real. So they all quit Jack and we made up a band. And I ran on the plan. And I just, and I ran on top. I mean, I did good. I did good. I did good. I did good all the way. What did you call it?
In them kinds. What about the Zulus? Did you play for them much? Oh, I played for the Zulus about seven or eight different years.
